identity.name: Linux crond Masquerade — the Shell Copied and Renamed to crond in a Scratch Directory, Then Run From That Path
identity.summary: The host's own shell is copied to a file named crond, and a second copy is renamed to crond, inside one scratch directory under /var/tmp. Both copies are then run from that path and start id, uname and hostname. Built for the built-in Cortex XDR Analytics alert 'Masquerading as the Linux crond process' (Low).
identity.description: Source: the Cortex XDR Analytics alert reference page for 'Masquerading as the Linux crond process', as it read on 2026-11-13. The page describes the alert in one sentence ('Copies a file and renames it as crond.') and lists: activation period 14 Days, training period 30 Days, test period N/A (single event), deduplication period 1 Day, required data XDR Agent, severity Low, ATT&CK tactic TA0005 Defense Evasion and technique T1036.004 Masquerading: Masquerade Task or Service. It publishes no trigger predicate, no threshold, no field name, no hash, no domain and no file path, and it names no actor and no campaign. Nothing on this card is attributed to one, and the card carries no indicator: every path and file name here is the scenario's own choice. WHAT SIM-EDR-026 DOES. All of it is real execution inside one hidden directory, /var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond. /var/tmp is world-writable, the name is predictable and the steps run as root, so step 1 removes the path and creates the directory itself (mkdir without -p, mode 0700) and stops if another user has put anything there; every later step reads the root's type, owner and mode in one stat call and stops unless it is a directory, owned by the running user, mode 700. The cleanup makes the same test before it reads the pidfile; when the test fails it skips the pidfile and still removes the path. Step 1 copies /bin/sh straight to copy/crond, and copies it again to renamed/sh-copy.tmp and renames that to renamed/crond: the two readings of the page's sentence. Step 2 runs copy/crond once in the foreground; that process, whose image name is crond, starts id, uname and hostname. Step 3 starts renamed/crond in the background; it runs the same three commands and then idles so that a process named crond is visible outside a system path for about 45 seconds. It ends itself after 300 seconds or when the sandbox is gone. Step 4 lists processes named crond through /proc, stops the instance by its pidfile and removes the sandbox. The cron service, crontabs, /etc/cron*, /usr/sbin/cron, systemd and the network are never touched; on Ubuntu the cron daemon is /usr/sbin/cron, so no file named crond is replaced or shadowed. Steps are spaced 40 s apart because back-to-back steps lost telemetry in the lab on 2026-11-11. WHAT IS DECLARED. Five step-detections: the built-in alert as one ABIOC row on step 1 (on the basis of the reference page; not yet observed in a lab run), three XQL validation rows that are scored only by Tier-2 verify, and one operator-installed correlation rule, CR-EDR-0026. The additional ATT&CK techniques on this card (T1036.003, T1059.004, T1033, T1082, T1057) are this card's own mapping of what the steps do, not the page's. The chain has not been run on the lab endpoint or against the tenant.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-EDR-026 — the shell copied and renamed to crond in a scratch directory and run from there, delivered by the CortexSim beacon as root or as a push bundle.

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR agent on the Linux endpoint (lab: 9.4.0.470 on Ubuntu 24.04, report mode).

/var/tmp allows execution. On the lab endpoint it does: a read-only probe on 2026-11-13 found /var/tmp on / without noexec, mode 1777, with fs.protected_symlinks=1. If it is mounted noexec, step 1 still copies and renames, step 2 exits 126 and a pull run stops there: the beacon is fail-fast and a pull run executes no cleanup, so six root-owned paths stay on the endpoint (/var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond, copy/, copy/crond, renamed/, renamed/crond, run/) until the next run's step 1 removes them or the operator does. That is an environment limit, not a missed detection.
prerequisites.remediation: Run the chain on an endpoint whose /var/tmp allows execution. To remove what a stopped pull run left behind, as root: if [ "$(stat -c %F:%u:%a /var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond 2>/dev/null)" = "directory:$(id -u):700" ] && [ -f /var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond/run/linger.pid ] && grep -q cortexsim-crond "/proc/$(cat /var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond/run/linger.pid)/cmdline" 2>/dev/null; then kill "$(cat /var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond/run/linger.pid)" 2>/dev/null; fi; rm -rf /var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond

prerequisites.description: Nothing owned by another user at /var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond. Step 1 removes the path and creates the directory with mkdir (no -p, mode 0700); if another local user re-creates it in between, step 1 exits non-zero. A pull run stops there. A push bundle goes on: each later step sleeps 40 s and exits 1 at its ownership check. That check is one stat call, and a step executes or reads nothing under the root unless the call says: a directory, owned by the running user, mode 700. All of this relies on /var/tmp being sticky (mode 1777 on the lab endpoint), which is what stops another user renaming or removing root's directory once step 1 has made it. Do not run the chain on a host whose /var/tmp is not sticky: there the check and the use are still two lookups of one path.

Stock tools: sh, mkdir, rm, cp, mv, chmod, ls, cat, grep, readlink, stat, sleep, id, uname and hostname. Bash and coreutils were read back from the lab endpoint, which covers all of these except grep and hostname; those two are not named in the read-back and are assumed from a stock Ubuntu 24.04 server install. A missing tool makes its step exit non-zero. No interpreter beyond the shell is needed.
prerequisites.check_command: for t in sh mkdir rm cp mv chmod ls cat grep readlink stat sleep id uname hostname; do command -v "$t" >/dev/null || exit 1; done

prerequisites.description: Correlation CR-EDR-0026 from this card installed in the tenant at Medium before the run, with issue suppression of 1 hour on the field agent_id and no MITRE tag. Without it the only alert-backed row left is the built-in alert, which has not been observed in a lab run.
prerequisites.check_command: echo 'confirm in the tenant console: Detection Rules > Correlations'

prerequisites.description: At least 75 minutes since the previous SIM-EDR-026 run was launched on this endpoint. Inside that time the earlier run's issue suppression is still active and delays the new run's issue; with no suppression, the rule looks back one hour on a 10-minute schedule and an issue raised for the earlier run's events is credited to the new run by rule name. The built-in alert is deduplicated for one day, so a second run within a day may raise no second issue.
prerequisites.check_command: echo 'confirm the launch time of the last SIM-EDR-026 run on this endpoint'

prerequisites.description: Root is how the lab delivers the steps (the lab endpoint has no service account). Nothing in the chain needs root: /var/tmp is world-writable and /bin/sh is world-readable.

payload.code:
# NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR THE SCENARIO: scenarios/edr/edr-026-crond-masquerade-from-scratch-path.yml is the delivery path (four steps, 40 s apart, with the checks, the lingering instance and its stop). This is the behaviour in brief.
set -eu
D=/var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond
# The root is created atomically: no -p, so mkdir fails if another user put anything at the path.
rm -rf "$D"; mkdir -m 700 "$D"; mkdir "$D/copy" "$D/renamed"
cp /bin/sh "$D/copy/crond"
cp /bin/sh "$D/renamed/sh-copy.tmp"; mv "$D/renamed/sh-copy.tmp" "$D/renamed/crond"
# Nothing under the root is executed unless ONE stat call says: a directory, owned by this user, mode 700.
[ "$(stat -c %F:%u:%a "$D" 2>/dev/null)" = "directory:$(id -u):700" ] || { echo "sandbox $D is missing or not ours: step-01 did not complete" >&2; exit 1; }
"$D/copy/crond" -c 'id; uname -a; hostname; echo done'
"$D/renamed/crond" -c 'id; uname -a; hostname; echo done'

expected_artifacts.description: The shell copied straight to the name crond by cp.
A second copy, written as sh-copy.tmp and renamed to crond by mv. FILE_RENAME has not been seen in this lab, so the mv process start is the dependable record.
A process whose image name is crond, started from the sandbox and not from a system directory (step 2 from copy/, step 3 from renamed/).
id, uname and hostname started by the crond-named process; in step 3 also one sleep child every five seconds while the instance idles.

cleanup.code:
# The pidfile is read only when one stat call says the root is a directory, owned by this user, mode 700. Otherwise it is skipped; the removal is unconditional.
if [ "$(stat -c %F:%u:%a /var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond 2>/dev/null)" = "directory:$(id -u):700" ] && [ -f /var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond/run/linger.pid ] && grep -q cortexsim-crond "/proc/$(cat /var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond/run/linger.pid)/cmdline" 2>/dev/null; then kill "$(cat /var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond/run/linger.pid)" 2>/dev/null; fi
rm -rf /var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond

abiocs.name: Masquerading as the Linux crond process
abiocs.description: PANW built-in XDR Analytics BIOC. Reference page: https://cortex-docs.paloaltonetworks.com/analytics-alerts/alerts-by-name/masquerading-as-the-linux-crond-process . As it read on 2026-11-13 the page states: description 'Copies a file and renames it as crond.'; activation period 14 Days; training period 30 Days; test period N/A (single event); deduplication period 1 Day (carried below as suppression_window_seconds 86400); required data XDR Agent; severity Low; ATT&CK TA0005 Defense Evasion, T1036.004 Masquerading: Masquerade Task or Service. It publishes no trigger predicate, threshold or field name. The name is the built-in alert name verbatim so the matcher keys on it. Reading a verdict: the matcher credits a row on the ATT&CK technique and on shared words as well as on the exact name. An Analytics BIOC issue with a different name on the same endpoint also marks the SIM-EDR-026 row detected when it is tagged with any T1036 technique or sub-technique, or when its name shares two words of four or more letters with that row's description. The row stands for this alert only when the verdict's alert name equals the name above (its matched_on list contains rule_name). SIM-EDR-026 declares it on step 1, the step that copies a file to the name crond and also copies and then renames one, because it is a single-event detector whose published trigger the lab can perform for real. It has not been observed in a lab run. Low: a Low issue never creates or joins a case. A declared row that no alert matches is held pending for the activation period and leaves the denominator, unless the tenant is attested soakless. The logic below is an approximation of the published sentence for hunting. It is not the built-in's code, and how the built-in decides is not published.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter (event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE_NEW, ENUM.FILE_WRITE, ENUM.FILE_RENAME) and action_file_name = "crond" and actor_process_image_name in ("cp", "mv"))
   or (event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START and action_process_image_name in ("cp", "mv") and action_process_image_command_line ~= "/crond[ ]*$")
abiocs.causality_anchor: The process that performs the copy or the rename (cp or mv) and its causality chain. In the lab that chain is the root step shell under the CortexSim beacon.

xql_queries.name: EDR-026 Crond Named File Created Or Renamed Under Var Tmp
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter timestamp_diff(current_time(), _time, "SECOND") < 3600
| filter (event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE_NEW, ENUM.FILE_WRITE, ENUM.FILE_RENAME) and action_file_path in ("/var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond/copy/crond", "/var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond/renamed/crond"))
   or (event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START and action_process_image_name in ("cp", "mv") and (action_process_image_command_line contains "/var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond/copy/crond" or action_process_image_command_line contains "/var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond/renamed/crond"))
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, actor_process_image_name, event_sub_type, action_file_path, action_process_image_command_line

xql_queries.name: EDR-026 Crond Named Process Started From Var Tmp
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter timestamp_diff(current_time(), _time, "SECOND") < 3600
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "crond" and action_process_image_path = "/var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond/copy/crond"
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_path, action_process_image_command_line

xql_queries.name: EDR-026 Crond Named Process Starts Discovery Children
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter timestamp_diff(current_time(), _time, "SECOND") < 3600
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("id", "uname", "hostname")
| filter actor_process_image_path = "/var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond/renamed/crond" or actor_process_command_line contains "/var/tmp/.cortexsim-crond/renamed/crond"
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, actor_process_image_name, actor_process_image_path, action_process_image_name, action_process_image_command_line

xql_queries.name: EDR-026 Hunt — Process Named Crond Running Off The System Path
xql_queries.query:
// Any Linux endpoint, last 24 hours. A process whose image name is crond that is not at /usr/sbin, /sbin, /usr/bin or /bin; add the path of any other packaged daemon first. Ubuntu and Debian name the daemon cron, so any hit there deserves a look.
dataset = xdr_data
| filter timestamp_diff(current_time(), _time, "SECOND") < 86400
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "crond" and action_process_image_path not in ("/usr/sbin/crond", "/sbin/crond", "/usr/bin/crond", "/bin/crond")
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_path, action_process_image_command_line, action_process_image_sha256

xql_queries.name: EDR-026 Hunt — Crond File Appears By Copy Or Move
xql_queries.query:
// Any Linux endpoint, last 24 hours. A file named crond appears outside /usr/sbin, /sbin, /usr/bin and /bin, or cp or mv is started with a destination that ends in /crond and is not one of those four. Package managers are left out. On RHEL-family hosts expect configuration files of the same name under /etc.
dataset = xdr_data
| filter timestamp_diff(current_time(), _time, "SECOND") < 86400
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter (event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE_NEW, ENUM.FILE_WRITE, ENUM.FILE_RENAME) and action_file_name = "crond" and action_file_path not in ("/usr/sbin/crond", "/sbin/crond", "/usr/bin/crond", "/bin/crond"))
   or (event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START and action_process_image_name in ("cp", "mv") and action_process_image_command_line ~= "/crond[ ]*$" and action_process_image_command_line !~= "[ ](/usr)?/s?bin/crond[ ]*$")
| filter actor_process_image_name not in ("dpkg", "rpm", "dnf", "yum", "apt-get")
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, actor_process_image_name, actor_process_command_line, event_sub_type, action_file_path, action_process_image_command_line

xql_queries.name: EDR-026 Hunt — What A Stray Crond Spawned, Per Endpoint
xql_queries.query:
// Any Linux endpoint, last 24 hours. What a crond-named process that is not at /usr/sbin, /sbin, /usr/bin or /bin started, per endpoint and per executable.
dataset = xdr_data
| filter timestamp_diff(current_time(), _time, "SECOND") < 86400
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name = "crond" and actor_process_image_path not in ("/usr/sbin/crond", "/sbin/crond", "/usr/bin/crond", "/bin/crond")
| comp count() as children, count_distinct(action_process_image_name) as distinct_children, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen by agent_hostname, agent_id, actor_process_image_path
| fields agent_hostname, agent_id, actor_process_image_path, children, distinct_children, first_seen, last_seen

xql_queries.name: EDR-026 Hunt — One Executable Hash Started Under A Shell Name And As Crond
xql_queries.query:
// Any Linux endpoint, last 24 hours. The same executable content started under a shell name and under the name crond: the renamed-binary shape, whatever the path. No hash value is written here; the query groups on the field.
dataset = xdr_data
| filter timestamp_diff(current_time(), _time, "SECOND") < 86400
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("crond", "sh", "dash", "bash", "busybox") and action_process_image_sha256 != null
| alter started_as_crond = if(action_process_image_name = "crond", 1, 0)
| comp count_distinct(action_process_image_name) as names, max(started_as_crond) as seen_as_crond, count() as starts, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen by agent_hostname, agent_id, action_process_image_sha256
| filter names >= 2 and seen_as_crond = 1

correlation_rules.name: EDR-026 Crond Lookalike Planted And Launched
correlation_rules.logic:
Operator-installed correlation rule (CortexSim never writes it to the tenant). Alert name EXACTLY as this rule's name; severity Medium (only Medium or higher opens or joins a case); Scheduled, every 10 minutes, query time frame 1 hour; Issue Suppression enabled, Duration time 1 hour, Fields agent_id; alert field mapping: agent_hostname -> Host Name, agent_id -> Agent ID (the mapped artifacts are what let a correlation issue join a case); NO MITRE tag (an issue tagged T1036 would also be credited to the validation rows of SIM-EDR-026 step 1 and step 2, because every row of a step shares the step's technique). UNTESTED: this XQL has not been run in any tenant. Its alter, comp, then filter shape follows CR-EDR-0023, which was tested read-only in the lab tenant on 2026-11-11; the not in comparisons and the !~= comparison were not part of that test. It is built only from process and file events SIM-EDR-026 produces on one host. No leg names the sandbox, so the rule matches the same behaviour at any path other than the four system paths it excludes: /usr/sbin/crond, /sbin/crond, /usr/bin/crond and /bin/crond. On a host whose packaged daemon lives anywhere else, ordinary cron activity gives the launched and spawned legs, so add that path to the three exclusion lists before enabling the rule tenant-wide. Three legs: planted (a file named crond is created, written or renamed outside the system paths, or cp or mv is started with a destination that ends in /crond and is not one of them), launched (a process whose image name is crond starts from outside the system paths) and spawned (a process is started by such a crond). It fires for one agent that shows at least two of the three, so one missing file sub-type does not silence it; SIM-EDR-026 produces all three. Repeats: the rule matches again on every scheduled run while the events stay inside the one-hour time frame. With the suppression above only the first match per agent_id raises an issue in that hour, so one run of SIM-EDR-026 gives one issue; that is the behaviour the product documentation describes for issue suppression and it has not been exercised in the lab. With suppression left off (the product default) one run gives up to six issues. There is no current_time in the rule: the time frame bounds it. XQL:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| alter leg = if(event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START and action_process_image_name = "crond" and action_process_image_path not in ("/usr/sbin/crond", "/sbin/crond", "/usr/bin/crond", "/bin/crond"), "launched", if(event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START and actor_process_image_name = "crond" and actor_process_image_path not in ("/usr/sbin/crond", "/sbin/crond", "/usr/bin/crond", "/bin/crond"), "spawned", if(event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START and action_process_image_name in ("cp", "mv") and action_process_image_command_line ~= "/crond[ ]*$" and action_process_image_command_line !~= "[ ](/usr)?/s?bin/crond[ ]*$", "planted", if(event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE_NEW, ENUM.FILE_WRITE, ENUM.FILE_RENAME) and action_file_name = "crond" and action_file_path not in ("/usr/sbin/crond", "/sbin/crond", "/usr/bin/crond", "/bin/crond"), "planted", "other"))))
| filter leg in ("planted", "launched", "spawned")
| comp count_distinct(leg) as legs, count() as events, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen by agent_hostname, agent_id
| filter legs >= 2

analytics_modules: Not declared: no multi-event, baseline XDR Analytics alert is an expectation of this chain. The Low built-in Analytics BIOCs seen on this endpoint for other chains ('Uncommon Linux shell command execution', 'Suspicious access to shadow file', 'Suspicious data encryption', 'UNIX LOLBIN process connected to a rare external host') are rarity-based, never join a case, and are not expectations here.

rule_ids: Masquerading as the Linux crond process
products.evidence_query: Issue 'Masquerading as the Linux crond process' on the endpoint (detection method ANALYTICS_BIOC, Low). Declared from the alert reference page; not yet observed in a lab run.

Issue 'EDR-026 Crond Lookalike Planted And Launched' (operator-installed correlation, Medium) on the endpoint. It is the only Medium-or-higher issue this chain can raise: one per run with the issue suppression this card specifies, a new one on every scheduled run while the events stay inside the hour without it.

threat_scenarios.name: A System Binary Copied And Renamed To crond, Then Run From A Scratch Path
threat_scenarios.description: Copy the shell to a file named crond, copy and rename a second one, run both from the scratch path, and show what Cortex XDR raises on the copy and what the telemetry holds for the process and its children.

threat_steps.objective: The copy and the rename to the name crond raise the built-in masquerading alert, and the file and process telemetry of both is recorded.
preconditions: Linux endpoint with the Cortex agent; built-in Analytics BIOCs enabled.
No firing of the same alert on this endpoint in the previous day (the alert is deduplicated for one day).
steps: Copy /bin/sh straight to a file named crond in the sandbox.
Copy /bin/sh under another name and rename it to crond.
success_criteria: Issue `Masquerading as the Linux crond process` (Low, method ANALYTICS_BIOC) on the endpoint.
XQL `EDR-026 Crond Named File Created Or Renamed Under Var Tmp` returns the cp or mv process start, or a file event on one of the two crond files.

threat_steps.objective: The crond-named process and its children are recorded from the scratch path, and the operator-installed correlation stitches the chain into one Medium issue.
preconditions: CR-EDR-0026 installed at Medium with issue suppression of 1 hour on agent_id and no MITRE tag.
steps: Run the first copy in the foreground; it starts id, uname and hostname.
Start the renamed copy in the background; it runs the same commands and idles.
List processes named crond through /proc, stop the instance and remove the sandbox.
success_criteria: XQL `EDR-026 Crond Named Process Started From Var Tmp` returns the process start.
XQL `EDR-026 Crond Named Process Starts Discovery Children` returns at least one of id, uname and hostname.
Issue `EDR-026 Crond Lookalike Planted And Launched` (Medium, method CORRELATION) on the endpoint.

preventive_controls: Mount /tmp, /var/tmp and /dev/shm noexec where the workload allows it, so a binary copied there cannot run under any name.
Keep an allow-list of where daemon binaries live. A process named after a daemon that runs from a user-writable directory is the thing to block or review.

Know the daemon's real name per distribution: Ubuntu and Debian run cron from /usr/sbin/cron, RHEL-family hosts run crond from /usr/sbin/crond. On an Ubuntu host a process named crond is unexpected at any path.
detection_engineering: Key on the pair of image name and image path, not on the name alone: crond from its packaged path is the daemon (/usr/sbin/crond on RHEL-family hosts, /usr/bin/crond on distributions that merge sbin into bin), crond from anywhere else is a copy. The rule and the hunts here exclude /usr/sbin, /sbin, /usr/bin and /bin; a daemon packaged elsewhere needs its path added.
A renamed binary keeps its content, so the same executable hash started under two image names is a path-independent signal; the fourth hunting query groups on that field.
FILE_RENAME has not been seen in this lab for files under /var/tmp, so the validation row and the correlation rule accept the cp or mv process start as well as the file event.
Use actor_causality_id, not a bare causality_id, and timestamp_diff(current_time(), _time, "SECOND") for time windows: the lab tenant rejected the other forms.
Every beacon-run step in the lab recorded cortexsim-agent as its causality actor, so no query here keys on the causality owner's name.
Keep the operator rule at Medium or higher and map agent_hostname and agent_id in its alert fields. The built-in alert is Low, and a Low issue never creates or joins a case.
Install CR-EDR-0026 with no MITRE tag. The matcher credits a tagged correlation issue to every XQL row on a step with the same technique, which would overstate Detection Accuracy.
Enable issue suppression on CR-EDR-0026 (1 hour, field agent_id). A scheduled rule whose time frame is longer than its schedule matches the same events on every run; suppression is off by default.

A scratch directory under a world-writable path is only safe for a root step when the step creates it itself, without -p, and every later step reads its type, owner and mode in one stat call before touching it. Separate tests are separate path lookups that another user can swap between. A predictable path that is merely re-used lets any local user plant what root then runs.
